I am 72, started farming when I was 22, never went to school. I got 20 mu, too much for just me and the old woman, so I hire the machine crew from the village for plowing and harvest. I keep 14 mu for wheat then corn, and 6 mu for cotton, same as last year. I don't trust new ideas from outside — I do what I did before, and I watch Old Wang and the others. If their wheat looks good, I sleep fine.

For wheat, I sow right after National Day with the improved seed everyone buys from the shop in town. At planting, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that's the one with the three numbers on it, 50 kilos a bag. Then when the wheat turns green in March, I broadcast almost a full bag of urea per mu. I know it costs money, but two years ago I listened to someone saying use less, and the heads came out small. I lost more on yield than I saved on fertilizer. Better waste a little fertilizer than cry over a bad harvest. I irrigate three times: the overwintering water, then at jointing, then when the grain is filling. I spray twice for weeds and bugs. The tractor does rotary tillage, quick and neat. I expect about 450 kilos per mu if the weather plays fair.

For corn, I plant right after cutting wheat in early June. Everyone uses hybrid seed now, you get big ears. I don't have time to plow — the season is short — so I no-till plant. I put half a bag of compound per mu at planting, then when the plants are knee-high I spread urea. Irrigate twice if the rain stays away. Spray twice. Should get 550 kilos per mu, maybe more.

For cotton, I plow deep in April and plant improved seed. Cotton needs potash, so I use one bag of compound plus extra potash fertilizer. I spray four times because the bollworms and aphids love cotton. Irrigate three times. Cotton is hard work, but last year's price was alright, so I keep my 6 mu. I hire people to help pick. Hope for 280 kilos of seed cotton per mu.

That's my plan. I don't change what works.
